Below is a minimal patch that fixes the most obvious piece of mis‐parsing in parsefiguredivs.lua.  In your original, any two‐image float was being treated as a single‐image float (because of the “<= 2” test), which in turn prevented the proper subfloat machinery (and auto‐ids) from ever kicking in.

With this change, only *exactly one* image is handled by the “simple figure” branch.  Any 2⁺ images now stay in the “multi” branch, which will allow Quarto’s subfloat logic (and the crossref filter) to assign sub‐IDs and emit `\subcaption{…}` correctly.

With that one change your two‐image floats will now remain in the “multi‐image” path, allowing Quarto’s built-in subfloat/CrossRef logic to:

  1. auto‐generate subfigure identifiers for each child,  
  2. place them in the same `figure` environment, and  
  3. render `\subcaption{\label{…}…}` rather than ordinary `\caption{…}`.  

That should restore the behaviour shown in your “patched” MWE.
